title: CReal.ivt_approx: the constructive approximate Intermediate Value Theorem -- roots to any requested accuracy
statement: CReal.ivt_approx is the general constructive form of the Intermediate Value Theorem, ADR-0603 row 1. Let F be an arbitrary uniformly continuous real function on [a, b], with F a <= 0 <= F b. Then for EVERY accuracy target n, there exists x in [a, b] with abs (F x) <= 1/(n+1) -- an approximate root to any requested accuracy, all from one proof, since F, a, b are arbitrary and n is universally quantified. This is not a special case of a stronger unstated theorem: CReal.ivt_exact_root_decides_sign shows that an EXACT root (Equiv (F x) zero, no epsilon) cannot be reached from these hypotheses alone, because doing so for an arbitrary F would decide the sign of an arbitrary real. What this fact does NOT state: the target value is fixed at zero (Mathlib's Icc (f a) (f b) subset f '' Icc a b covers every intermediate value, not just a root -- reachable here via CReal.uniformly_continuous_sub/const but not registered as its own fact); the orientation is fixed at F a <= 0 <= F b (the reverse is reachable via CReal.uniformly_continuous_neg, also unregistered); and the hypothesis is UNIFORM continuity with an explicit modulus, not Mathlib's pointwise ContinuousOn -- this kernel has no pointwise-continuity predicate at all, so that gap cannot even be stated here.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.ivt_approx : ((x0 : ((x0 : CReal) -> CReal)) -> ((x1 : CReal) -> ((x2 : CReal) -> ((x3 : CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn x0 x1 x2) -> ((x4 : CReal.le x1 x2) -> ((x5 : CReal.le (x0 x1) CReal.zero) -> ((x6 : CReal.le CReal.zero (x0 x2)) -> ((x7 : AxNat) -> Exists.{1} CReal (fun (x8 : CReal) => And (CReal.le x1 x8) (And (CReal.le x8 x2) (CReal.le (CReal.abs (x0 x8)) (CReal.ofRat (Rat.natDivSucc (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero) x7)))))))))))))

evidence.supports: CReal.ivt_approx is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example theorem_dependency_inventory -- CReal.ivt_approx 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^CReal\.ivt_approx[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: Two independent failure modes, so the exit status depends on the finding rather than on the run completing: theorem_dependency_inventory exits non-zero when a NAMED filter matches nothing, and grep -c exits 1 printing 0 when the anchored line is absent. Anchored with [[:space:]], never \t -- in a scripted (GNU) grep \t is a literal t. grep -c rather than grep -q, which would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail. --release is MANDATORY: this tool builds creal/complex/cpoint, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

provenance.source: Derived mechanically from the unfiltered emit of `cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection`, which prints one TSV row per declaration whose fields are (prelude, kind, display name, axiom-footprint size, direct type declarations, direct declarations, direct theorems, Kernel::render_lean(declaration.ty())). formal.statement is that last field verbatim; depends_on is the direct-theorem column intersected with this ledger's registered facts; axiom_footprint is the footprint-size column, cross-checked by the whole-prelude nat_axiom_inventory run recorded in the second evidence row. No field was hand-transcribed and no prose was authored.

notes: CReal.ivt_approx is the closing statement of creal/ivt.rs's constructive approximate IVT construction (Spivak, Calculus ch. 7). It composes CReal.ivt_iter against the continuity modulus CReal.UniformlyContinuousOn supplies and an Archimedean bound on the initial width; see that module's own documentation for the full paper argument, including why a bisection maintaining a WEAK, epsilon-slack sign invariant (rather than the classical exact F P <= 0 <= F Q) is what lets the case split at each step come from cotransitivity on a fixed strict pair rather than from an undecidable comparison against zero. The three restrictions relative to Mathlib's `intermediate_value_Icc` (fixed target, fixed orientation, uniform vs. pointwise continuity) are recorded in docs/formalized-math-2026-08/08-ivt-and-evt-measured-against-mathlib.md, which found the first two reachable as cheap instantiations from lemmas already in the environment and the third a genuine, unstateable-here boundary. Source: crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/creal/ivt.rs.
